# Integrations Follow-up Plan (1.41.0)

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. **Every row begins by verifying its premise at HEAD**: a row closed at HEAD is a result to report, not a reason to build, and a carried verdict is a reading with a date — re-take it before quoting it. Most of Phase 6 is exactly that: carried verdicts whose value is the REASON, not the conclusion.

**Goal:** carry, without losing anything, what the 1.40.0 release deliberately did not ship — (1) the authorization work that must still be finished for a user who cannot open a browser, plus the two dp-auth rows whose rig-day precondition the owner has now met; (2) the codex quota build the owner decided by integration kind; (3) the two hooks/automations residues the owner sent to be built; (4) the owner decisions still pending; (5) the rig rows whose preconditions are now decided; and (6) a MEASURED-NULL REGISTER — one row per open measure row whose last drive recorded a null, carrying the reason it was null and what would change it, so that a row nobody can drive today is a readable fact rather than a silent gap.

**Born:** 2026-09-18, from the owner's release criterion of ~16:05 — *"в этом релизе не должно быть критичных багов; мелочи в следующий"* — and the owner decision round of ~16:40 recorded in the project memory file `owner-decisions-2026-09-18-followup-1-41-0.md` (items 1–6). The controller's instruction to write it now, ~17:05: *"составь уже план — если упадём по лимиту, важно ничего не потерять"*. Nothing here is re-decided: every row carries the owner decision it executes, or records that no decision has been asked for yet.

**Sequencing:** this plan runs AFTER the close-out of `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-10-integrations-and-authorization.md` and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-22-dp-auth-wave2-and-mcp-exposure.md`. **Those two plans stay in the tree and keep their trackers** — a finished plan is never deleted, and the deviations' reasons live there. At their close-out the controller MOVES each open row into this plan with a note per moved row (`moved to F1.n`), the glyph kept; until that commit lands, the rows referenced below are still theirs and this file only points at them. Within this plan the phase order is the wave order: Phase 1 and Phase 2 are the first wave, Phase 3 the second, Phase 5's rig rows ride the sittings, Phase 6 is a register that is re-read rather than executed, and Phase 7 is the close-out.

**Architecture:** unchanged. The base agent stays host-side (SessionManager + session-tools + the shared pipeline); Pi is built to Claude Code's documentation; capability variance is DATA, never renderer branches. Three standing rules govern every row and are carried BY REFERENCE rather than restated — **Native-first, and the host is the smooth seam**; **Read, do not invent**; **the balance rule**. Two of them decide rows here by name: Phase 2's split by integration kind is native-first (a subscription card reads the runtime's own windows; a gateway card reads the budget the host already reads), and Phase 1's refusal to parse output that does not exist is read-don't-invent.

**Readers of this file, stated so nobody is surprised:**

- `python3 scripts/sort-plan-tracker.py <this file> --check` reads the tracker and must stay green. Every `F1.n` row sorts on `n` alone, so the row numbers ASCEND with the phases: a row inserted into an earlier phase later takes the next free number and is placed by its phase heading, not by its id.
- `python3 scripts/sort-plan-tracker.py --shas` (the `lint:plan-shas` step of `lint:chain`) reads EVERY plan: each commit cell must name a real commit or an em dash, and each `|` inside a cell must be escaped as a backslash-pipe — an unescaped one makes the row MISALIGNED and its shas go unchecked.
- `python3 scripts/plan-status.py` does **not** read this plan; it is pinned to `2026-08-22-runtime-parity-closure.md` in its own source. Count this tracker's rows directly.
- `python3 scripts/build-parity-report.py` reads the FULL TEXT of every plan under `docs/superpowers/plans/` as a directory glob, so this file moves its section 3 the moment it lands. The controller regenerates it at close-out from a clean tree; do not regenerate it from a lane.
- `bun scripts/check-doc-anchors.ts` treats any `<word>.md#<word>` as a citation. This file deliberately names upstream pages IN WORDS for that reason; keep it that way when you add a row.

## Phase 0 — Read-me

Prose only; this phase has no tracker rows. It exists because every row below was written against facts that a reader six weeks from now cannot reconstruct from the row alone.

**The release that precedes this plan.** 1.40.0 shipped under the owner's criterion of 2026-09-18 ~16:05: *no critical bugs* — a user must be able to use the app and every runtime correctly — and *small things go to the next release*. That criterion is why this plan exists and why most of it is features and measurements rather than fixes. Three release blockers (the `mcp__session__remember` hang on claude and codex, Stop not interrupting a claude turn behind a queued message, and the trust modal on a deleted directory) were fixed in 1.40.0 and are NOT carried here.

**How this plan was seeded.** From the owner decision round of 2026-09-18 ~16:40, items 1–6, in that order: (1) headless dp sign-in, (2) rig-day environments, (3) codex rate-limit windows by integration kind, (4) the two hooks residues, (5) the NULL measure rows as one register, (6) *"auth must work correctly for the user — do everything we can now, defer the rest to the other plan"*. Item 1's option 1a was REFUTED by research lane RQ-dp-device before this file was written; Phase 1 records the refutation and the routes that survive it, which is why Phase 1 does not look like the memory file's item 1.

**The credential hand-over recipe — read it before any row that needs a key or an account.** Three rows need a credential this repository must never see: F1.4 and F1.13 need an entitled model key of the owner's, F1.8 needs the owner's personal ChatGPT/Codex subscription. The recipe, stated to the owner by the controller and binding on every lane:

1. The owner adds the BYO connection, or performs the subscription login, THEMSELVES, in the app's own connection UI, in a DEDICATED rig profile — a `NESSY_CONFIG_DIR` of its own, launched with the `env -u` launcher that `scripts/cdp/README.md` prescribes (a sitting lane's shell exports names this product reads; a bare launch hands every one of them to the app).
2. A sitting COPIES that profile directory; it never re-enters the credential and never reads the credential file.
3. Nothing is printed, echoed, pasted into a report, or committed. A row's evidence is a length, a boolean, a verdict — never a value. A row that cannot be evidenced without quoting a secret is a row that stays unmeasured, and says so.

**The standing constraints** are AGENTS.md's §Editing Rules and §Traps plus Part 3 of `nessy-wf-checkpoints/work/reports/2026-09-18-handoff.md` (the hand-off), which states them verbatim and in force. The three that bite hardest in this plan: commit ONLY as `git commit -F <msgfile> -- <pathspec>`; a NEW file only by the new-file recipe; `./` on every path handed to `bun test`, and read the FILE COUNT of every run.

## Phase 1 — Auth that must work for the user (`F1.1`–`F1.5`)

The owner's words for this phase are *"auth must work correctly for the user — do everything we can now, defer the rest to the other plan"*. What could be done now was done in 1.40.0; this phase is the rest.

**The premise this phase was born under is REFUTED, and that is its most valuable finding.** Owner option 1a asked whether the `dp` CLI itself falls back to the RFC 8628 device flow when no browser can open — if so, our non-interactive branch would run `dp auth login` and relay the printed URL and code, at zero protocol cost. Research lane RQ-dp-device measured the shipped `dp` 13.50.0 (`spirit-core/spirit-cli` at `4c92725c`, `spirit-iam/iam` v5.10.1) against source clones pinned to the binary's own build metadata and answered **no**:

- No first-party source in the shipped tree contains a device flow at all. The only user login `dp` implements is authorization-code + PKCE, opening a browser and waiting on a loopback callback at `localhost:25565`.
- The RFC 8628 symbols visible in the binary are DEAD LIBRARY CODE from `golang.org/x/oauth2` v0.31.0, retained by the Go linker and structurally unable to run: the device-auth URL field of the OAuth endpoint is never assigned in any of the five first-party modules, so the first statement a call would execute returns an `endpoint missing` error — a string that is also in the binary.
- Headless, `dp` prints `opening browser tab for user to authorize...`, **never prints the authorization URL on any path**, silently discards the browser-open failure (on darwin the system opener exits 0 even over SSH, so there is no failure signal at all), and blocks until our own five-minute login timeout kills it.

So **there is nothing for a non-interactive branch to relay**, and the existing refusal is already the honest behaviour. The one lever that exists is the `BROWSER` environment variable, which `dp`'s opener prepends to its candidate list and invokes with the authorization URL as its first argument.

**What 1.40.0 already shipped, referenced and NOT carried as a row:** option B, the diagnostic half — the invisible-browser timeout now says what actually happened and where the callback must land — is row `DA3.17` of the dp-auth plan, lane WI-bi, in the release that precedes this one. Do not re-create it.

`F1.1` sends the seven platform-team questions and sequences FIRST, because `F1.3` is conditional on their answers and `F1.2` is a product posture one of them asks about. `F1.4` and `F1.5` are the two dp-auth rows the owner moved here by name.

## Phase 2 — Codex quota by integration kind (`F1.6`–`F1.8`)

**Owner decision 2026-09-18 ~16:40, item 3: build (b), BY INTEGRATION KIND.** A non-BYO (gateway) codex card reads the llm-proxy quota the typed `/quota` already reads for the Pi gateway card; a personal subscription card reads the subscription's own windows through codex's native `account/rateLimits/read` plus the `account/rateLimits/updated` notification, whose types are already generated in `packages/codex-protocol/generated/v2/`.

This is native-first with both halves named. The runtime HAS the mechanism for a subscription — and the host has measured, twice, that it refuses without one: at `codex-app-server 0.150.1` behind our loopback adapter with a synthetic key, `account/rateLimits/read` and `account/usage/read` both answer `-32600 codex account authentication required`, `account/read` answers a null account, the boot carries no `account/rateLimits/updated` notification, and the proxy sink recorded ZERO attempts — so the refusal is local and structural, not a network failure. The host does NOT have a mechanism for a subscription and never will. Conversely the gateway card is metered by the same per-user limiter as the Pi gateway card, and the host already reads that budget; what blocks the read is a deliberate posture, not an absence.

Two seams, named so a lane does not go looking: `packages/shared/src/agent/backend/composer-capabilities.ts` symbol `offersNestorQuota` gates `/quota` on the RUNTIME (the decision `gateway-quota-pointer.test.ts` pins as a negative control in both directions), and `packages/shared/src/agent/backend/internal/nestor-quota.ts` is the llm-proxy reader. The codex measurement and its refusal sentence are pinned in `packages/shared/src/agent/__tests__/codex-quota-window.test.ts`, which pins A SENTENCE and the ABSENCE of the calls — read its header before changing either.

## Phase 5 — Rig rows whose preconditions are now decided (`F1.13`–`F1.20`)

Every row here failed to be driven for a NAMED reason, and the owner decision round settled five of those reasons. What changed:

- **The owner's own key** (item 2.2) unblocks the vision arm and, on the same key, Phase 1's `F1.4`.
- **A separate macOS user account** (item 2.3, deciding the long-open fake-`HOME` question) unblocks the two rows whose rig needs a HOME the product's credential path does not follow. The alternative — a HOME override knob in the shipped product — is REFUSED as a new security surface, and that refusal is the decision, not a deferral.
- **The owner's personal subscription** (item 2.5) is Phase 2's measurement and is tracked there.
- **Windows, Linux and Azure DevOps stay PARKED** (items 2.1 and 2.4) until the channel or the host exists. A parked row is carried with its reason so that the day the channel reopens, nobody re-derives the rig.

One row here is buildable rather than blocked: `F1.16` needs a stub upstream that drops mid-response, which is a fixture this repository can write.

## Phase 6 — The measured-NULL register (`F1.21`–`F1.53`)

**Owner decision 2026-09-18 ~16:40, item 5 (option 5c):** close the refuted rows now, move the rest here as ONE register with reasons. Two rows were closed as refuted in the release that precedes this plan and are deliberately NOT registered: the claude push-notification row (the SDK we ship declares no such tool — the name occurs zero times in its type declarations, with two sibling tool names as the controls) and the agent-reload row (the reload symbol scores zero files and zero occurrences at HEAD against a loaded-definitions family at fifteen, so the row's own premise IS the finding).

**What a row here is, and what it is not.** Each row carries: the origin row id, the one-line subject, the MEASURED REASON the last drive recorded, and WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT — a rig, a lift, or an owner decision. It is not a backlog item waiting for a free afternoon: several of these are structurally undrivable on the artefact we ship, and saying so precisely is the deliverable. A register row closes when its reason stops being true, and the row names the event that would do it.

**Not registered here, and why.** Two families of open rows are excluded because they are not this plan's to carry:

1. **The current release's own work** — the CDP-case conversion row, the four defect rows fixed in 1.40.0, the README correction, the case-detector row and the permission-picker row (the `D1.356`, `D1.359`–`D1.364`, `D1.368`, `D1.369` family). They close with that release.
2. **The rows measure sitting 6 is driving as this plan is written** — `D1.66`, `D1.73`, `D1.75`, `D1.67`, `D1.82`, `D1.55`, `D1.58`, `D1.72`, `D1.68`, `D1.131` through `D1.138`, and `D1.177`. **Re-check every one of them at the integrations plan's close-out:** a row that sitting 6 drove is closed there and never reaches this file; a row it did not reach is added here as a register row, in sorted position, by the recipe. `D1.136` is the one overlap — it appears in Phase 5 as a rig row AND in sitting 6's list; if sitting 6 closes it, `F1.17` closes as already-done at the move.

**A standing caution for anyone re-driving one of these.** Most of the SIT-5b family share ONE sentence — *not drivable on this artefact, premise re-taken at HEAD with a control* — and that sameness is not laziness: the premises were re-taken individually, each with a positive control on the same instrument (a fabricated symbol scoring zero in the same file), and where a re-take MOVED a number the row says so. Read the sitting narrative under `docs/testing/cdp-runs/` before quoting a count from a row.

The asymmetry: the product resolves a worktree to its MAIN CHECKOUT for repository-scoped permission rules (following the permissions page) and does NOT for project identity (device + inode), so a developer who trusts a repository and enables a plugin for it meets an untrusted, plugin-less project the moment they add a worktree, while their don't-ask-again rules follow them there. Size S once decided. done_means: the owner's answer recorded here, the option implemented, and the dialog text updated if (c). Zone `packages/shared/src/projects/**` + the capability policy store. Nearest documented solution = Claude Code: workspace trust is asked per DIRECTORY, while project-scope plugin enablement lives in the repository's own settings and therefore travels into every worktree. So activation unifies on the main checkout and trust is asked once more in the worktree; option (a) is refused because it transfers whole-project trust into a directory the user never approved (a safety posture this row must not change quietly). CONTROLS: a real `git worktree add` — the plugin enabled for the repo is effective-active and mounted in the worktree, and the trust prompt appears there once; an unrelated directory gets neither. Trust is never read, and trusting the checkout leaves the worktree 'unknown' (asked once more). The CLI's `init` came 17 ms after its `task_notification` (61 ms in an earlier reading), before the send. Residue (→ P-WJ-am-1): a send inside that 17–61 ms window still lands in the new slot. LIVE (release sitting SIT-p, packaged `5896a66d2`, 2026-09-25; `work/sitting/SIT-p/verdicts.md`): the in-turn race was NOT hit — on the gateway the CLI's own answer to a background completion lands in under 1 s (faster than a 0.7 s poll); every follow-up after the own turn got its own reply, nothing stuck in the queue, button back to Send. |

The problem: F1.509's `runtimeOwnTurn` settled only on a `result` that arrived with no slot open. `sendMessage` checks this marker once, before its long preparation. The host write was ungated and came 400 ms after the own turn's slot-less `init`. - **Own turn with a tool call still to come, before the fix:** the CLI folded the host text into its running turn. The next request carried the text as a system-reminder: "This is how Claude Code surfaces messages the user sends mid-turn — within the running turn, often alongside the next tool result, rather than as a separate conversation turn." One `result` arrived, and it landed in the host slot. `runtimeOwnTurnSettled()` was still pending 11 s later. That is the wedge. - **Control, a plain own turn:** there was no fold. The CLI's reply landed in the host slot (the known slip), the host text ran as the child's next turn with no slot open, and that turn's `result` settled the marker to `null`. The fix, in `claude-agent.ts`: - `routeLiveMessage` now settles the own turn on any `result`, before the slot check. - The own turn is **not** superseded when a host slot opens. A slot that closes before the own turn's `result` (after a Stop or a source activation) would otherwise leave the child mid-turn with the marker already `null`. - The own turn has a limit: `CLAUDE_RUNTIME_OWN_TURN_BOUND_MS` (15 minutes). See "Product decisions stated" below. - When the limit expires, the promise settles, so `replayQueueWhenRuntimeTurnSettles` replays the queue. If no host turn is open, one latched warning tells the user at the start of the turn that then runs. - The limit lives with the promise, not in `SessionManager`. A host-only timer cannot end the wedge, because `sendMessage` reads the same pending promise again and queues on it again. Three details the page does not spell out were reimplemented from the vendored 2.1.267 runtime's behaviour, paraphrase only: local `$ref` branches are resolved, the first definition of a repeated property wins, and a property name the API would refuse is left out. The rig was a preloaded interceptor with a `Bun.serve` SSE upstream that records its own cancel. - `fetch(new Request(url, { signal }))` and `fetch(new Request(url), { signal })` both left the upstream stream open 1.5 s after the abort, and the reader stayed pending. It extends WJ-bj's R2a/R2b arms and ran in a throwaway sandbox, with HOME and NESSY_CONFIG_DIR exported inside it before bun started. `skills: ['real']` was the control. Findings: - An explicit selection FOLLOWED every skill-folder link. An absolute link and a relative link out of the workspace both exported the target's files. A link to the workspace root exported the whole workspace as one skill, `config.json` included. - `'all'` DROPPED every link without a warning, inside ones too, because its listing kept only `Dirent.isDirectory()`. The loader's `isSkillDirEntry` follows a link to a folder on purpose. - A `skills/` folder that is itself a link out of the workspace exported through both paths. - Selecting a FILE under `skills/` threw ENOTDIR from the whole export. The fix is in `exportSkills` only: - `'all'` now lists what the loader lists: a folder, or a link to one. `isSkillFolderEntry` mirrors `isSkillDirEntry` instead of importing it, so the loader file is untouched. - Every entry is resolved with `realpathSync`. It must lie strictly below the workspace's own real path (`isStrictlyInside`). Otherwise it is skipped with `skills[i]: does not resolve inside the workspace, skipping`, which never names the skill or the target. - A selected non-folder is skipped with `Skill '<name>' is not a folder, skipping`. - Files are read from the checked real path, not back through the link. DECIDED under the transparent-and-simple rule: 1. Containment is checked on the REAL path. A link anywhere on the way therefore counts, including `skills/` itself. A check on the last link only would leave the same outside read reachable one level up. 2. The workspace root is not "inside", because a link to it would export the whole workspace. 3. A dangling link and a link to a file are still dropped from `'all'` without a warning, as the loader drops them. A selected dangling link is still reported "not found". Links INSIDE a skill folder were never followed and still are not. `collectDirectoryFiles` keeps only real files and directories, and the test pins this. PREMISE CORRECTED: the skills on a fresh Nessy profile come from ~/.agents/skills, not from the operator's ~/.claude. Evidence from code and docs (neither directory was read): the host's global layer reads GLOBAL_AGENT_SKILLS_DIR = join(homedir(), '.agents', 'skills') (skills/storage.ts:34) as the 'home' skill tier (capabilities/native-sources.ts:2062, trust boundary in the header at :10-11); it is HOME-rooted, so an isolated NESSY_CONFIG_DIR does not remove it, which is why a fresh profile still lists them. The home ~/.claude is read only by the explicit Claude-setup importer (claude-setup-import.ts header: the GLOBAL scope reads CONFIG_DIR and ~/.agents/skills, NOT the home ~/.claude). The claude child gets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR = <workspaceRoot>/claude-config, assigned unconditionally (agent/options.ts:422 and :513), and its native Skill tool is disallowed (CLAUDE_SESSION_DISALLOWED_TOOLS, claude-agent.ts:1079), so claude's own Personal root (skills.md#where-skills-live: '~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md'; '.agents' occurs 0 times on the page, curl 2026-09-26) never reaches it. Two of three runtimes read ~/.agents/skills themselves: codex at the pinned rust-v0.156.1 (codex-protocol/manifest.json) in codex-rs/ext/skills/src/host_roots.rs lines 24-25 and 103-106 (home_dir.join(AGENTS_DIR_NAME).join(SKILLS_DIR_NAME) as SkillScope::User, raw fetch HTTP 200); Pi 0.85.1 in dist/core/package-manager.js:1976 (join(getHomeDir(), '.agents', 'skills')) with trust-manager.js:147 'always treated as a trusted user resource', which we switch off (noSkills: true, pi-agent-server/src/compat/pi-runtime-adapter.ts:501) because the host supplies it. The host tier makes claude the same. /workflow-authoring is our bundled skill (apps/electron/resources/skills/workflow-authoring). WHAT THE 28 ARE (code): the card's count is getSessionCapabilityInventory = managed.lastWithheldCapabilities = toAgentRuntime().withheld (capabilities/views.ts:214-265), one row per capability with the FIRST failing test: disabled (source-disabled, managed-denied, session-not-selected folder or API source, session-disabled), review-required, blocked, unsupported-runtime. '81 active' is the workspace catalog of ALL kinds minus the withheld keys (activeCapabilityNames, SessionCapabilityInventoryNotice.tsx), not a skill count. Prior reading: RS-97 on packaged 1.40.0 got 27 such rows, all MCP servers and capabilities (scripts/cdp/cases/rs-97.ts:39-41), so the 28 are most likely not the skills (hypothesis). RECIPE for the final sitting (packaged build, launched by scripts/cdp/README.md's env -u launcher, dark theme): (1) open a claude-gateway session and run one turn (the record is empty before the first resolution); take k = activeSession(s) from scripts/cdp/lib/state.ts. (2) w = await s.call('return await window.electronAPI.getSessionCapabilityInventory(' + JSON.stringify(k.sessionId) + ')'); positive control: w.length equals the 'N did not load' number in [data-testid=session-capability-summary]. (3) group w by kind and reason; write each group's count with its logicalName and pluginKey. (4) c = (await window.electronAPI.capabilities.getCatalog({ workspaceId: k.workspaceId })).capabilities; for every withheld key read its catalog row's unavailableReason and trustState (splits 'disabled'); check that c.length minus the withheld keys present in c equals the '81 active' number. (5) premise control through the product: c.filter(x => x.kind === 'skill' and x.key starts with 'skill::global::-::-::home::') is the ~/.agents/skills tier and must cover the /gsd-* palette entries; c.some(x => x.logicalName === 'innersource') must be false (the decision's ~/.claude-only control). (6) repeat (2)-(4) on a pi and a codex session in the SAME workspace: toAgentRuntime is shared, so only unsupported-runtime rows may differ. (7) verdict per group: expected (a folder or API source not selected for the session, a user OFF, a plugin awaiting trust review, a component the runtime cannot run) or a defect, which becomes a new row. Record it as a case row in docs/testing/cdp-live-checklist.md. (L5F2, RC4, 2026-10-11) the 7-step recipe for the 28 withheld capabilities driven on all three runtimes — inventories BYTE-IDENTICAL across pi/claude/codex (28 rows, all builtin:mcp source-disabled), the arithmetic 109−28=81 confirmed, the home tier = 73 = the machine's skills, the ~/.claude premise's correction product-confirmed; group verdict EXPECTED, no defect; the recipe is committed as sitting case RS-119. |

DEFERRED (owner 2026-09-25). (DN-041, 2026-09-26) FIXED arm 1. Cause: GuardianConsultState.consult cached every verdict per (action, cwd) for the session, failure-tagged ones included, so one transient judge failure (timeout, spawn-error, malformed, aborted, a throwing or empty port) replayed as a card for that exact action without asking the judge again. Fix: only a judge DECISION is cached (no_objection, deny, or an honest unsure); a failure never enters the cache. Read, not invented: Claude's classifier treats such failures as transient (errors.md#auto-mode-cannot-determine-the-safety-of-an-action, 'Rate-limited, overloaded, and server errors are transient, and retrying works'). Arm 2 REFUTED at HEAD (no reachable state): pi-agent awaits consult before any card is raised (consultGuardianForBorderline, consultGuardianDenyNet), and the runner aborts the judge at its budget, which since F1.256 is the judge child's own 60 s deadline, so no verdict arrives after a card is up; not built. Cost stated: a judge that keeps failing is asked again on each repeat of the same action, the price a distinct action already pays. core/__tests__/guardian-consult.test.ts RED 32/6 then GREEN 38/0 (1 file; 6 failure shapes re-judge; CONTROL deny and honest unsure stay cached); pi-agent-guardian-consult.test.ts 168/0 (1 file); typecheck:shared 0; eslint rc 0; git diff --check clean; guardian-consult.ts keeps 430 lines. |

MEASURE the model's own compound Bash under a structural allow rule first (Pi, claude; codex if the host evaluates it). CONTROL: a structural DENY rule still denies an unparseable command; floors still deny; a parseable command still matches as today. Claude unaffected (it evaluates no readable permission rules — see F1.813). `matchesRule` `case 'bash'` now asks `unparseableStructuralBashVerdict(rule.action)`: deny → the same final refusal, ask → an ask naming the rule, allow → no match (falls through to the next rule / the mode's default). Tokenizer unchanged, splittable commands judged as before, floors still deny. Stated consequence: in bypass an unsplittable command an unrelated allow rule used to refuse now runs, as with no rule. Suite 29/4 → 33/0; after-fix probes (Pi, codex, hook runner) behave as with no rule. |

The host posture is already uniform: cancelProcessing pauses a non-empty queue for every backend (D1.376) and onProcessingStopped drains only an unpaused one. The sitting's own files show it on Pi: SIT3-c session c1310151 (pi-api-key, the RS-103 arm F drive behind the side note) logged mid-stream send behavior queue, then Cancelling processing, then no second Starting chat until the app stopped 9 min later; its session.jsonl keeps the message isQueued and the header carries messageQueuePaused true. The false reading came from RS-103 arm F, which counted any user row carrying RS103QUEUED as drained, and a queued message is a user row from the moment it is submitted. Arm F now requires the message to be queued before the Stop, reads isQueued and the host queueGet 20 s after the Stop through stopQueueVerdict (kept-paused, sent, unpaused, lost), expects kept-paused, and resumes as the control.
